submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as it provides the best pion/kaon separation performance at 10 GeV/c while meeting all constraints. Key findings:

1. Performance: R3 achieves 4.029σ separation, which is 38.7% better than the next best option (R2 at 2.905σ). This substantial improvement in separation power is critical for hadron identification efficiency and purity.

2. Aging compliance: R3 passes the humidity aging test with transparency loss below 10%, ensuring long-term operational stability without replacement during the 10-year run. R1 fails this critical requirement and is eliminated.

3. Optimal thickness: The 3 cm thickness represents the optimal point for R3, maximizing separation while remaining well within the 1-6 cm constraint. Thinner or thicker configurations yield inferior performance (e.g., 1 cm: 3.375σ, 6 cm: 2.785σ).

4. Comparison: While R2 also passes aging requirements, its best separation (2.905σ at 3 cm) is significantly inferior to R3, making it unsuitable when the goal is to achieve the best possible separation.

The recommendation satisfies all hard constraints and delivers superior performance for the RICH detector application.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3 cm delivers 4.029σ separation, the highest among all viable candidates and thicknesses tested. This is 38.7% better than R2 (2.905σ).

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year humidity aging test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R3 passes the aging test (R3_passes_aging_test = 1), while R1 fails (R1_passes_aging_test = 0). Only 2 of 3 candidates pass this requirement.
Recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.
